correctness.rationale: The Hasse-derivative congruences H_j(c)=0 for j<i exactly characterize membership in C_i=((x+1)^i) in F_2[x]/(x^32-1), because x^32-1=(x+1)^32. For i<=11 the 11-bit syndrome/last-two-bits dynamic program counts each 32-bit word once, accumulating 30 ordinary triples and two cyclic wrap triples; for i>=12 distinct messages of degree <32-i yield all and only the 2^(32-i) words. The actual verify.c implements these recurrences and elementwise comparison with actual SPECTRUM.csv; the separate crosscheck.py handles both sides i=11/12. I inspected the C transitions, Gray updates and supplied CSV. Independently enumerated all messages for i=16,20,24,28,30,31,32; obtained A_16,32=17155 and the published minimum-weight counts for these rows. The program is a finite exhaustive algorithm, not an extrapolation; the complete 33-row C program was not independently rerun in this execution, so the remaining CSV coefficients rely on the inspected exhaustive code and existing package verification.
